title: Make Two Arrays Equal by Reversing Subarrays
summary: Given two equal-length integer arrays target and arr, you can reverse any non-empty subarray of arr any number of times.
statement: Given two equal-length integer arrays target and arr, you can reverse any non-empty subarray of arr any number of times. Determine if arr can be made identical to target.
constraints: Any subarray may be reversed any number of times.
Return whether arr can become target.
hints: A length-two reversal swaps adjacent elements.
Adjacent swaps generate any permutation, so only the multiset matters.
Compare value frequencies in target and arr.
Equal counters are sufficient by permutation reachability and necessary because reversal never changes values.
editorial: Equal counters are sufficient by permutation reachability and necessary because reversal never changes values.

tests.explanation: The arrays contain the same multiset, and reversals can realize any permutation.
The multiplicity of one and two differs, so conversion is impossible.
